title: Personal error log
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lessons 11, 21, 43, 45 (Personal error log (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 11: Technical accuracy: punctuation for control. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Fix
Example
rows: The rain stopped, the street was silent.
The rain stopped. The street was silent.
The rain stopped; the street was silent.
When the rain stopped, the street was silent.

head: Possession
Omission
rows: never for plurals: apples, not apple's

keywords.def: two sentences wrongly joined with only a comma
words spoken by characters, in speech marks

questions.q: Fix: 'I opened the door, the room was empty.'
questions.a: I opened the door. The room was empty. (or a semi-colon, or 'When I opened the door, the room was empty.')

questions.q: Punctuate: where are you going said Gran dont be late
questions.a: 'Where are you going?' said Gran. 'Don't be late.'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, correct the 12 errors in the paragraph on the pupil PDF, then write a 6-line dialogue with correct punctuation. Starter: 'Don't open it,' ...
questions.a: All 12 errors fixed (splices, apostrophes, speech) and a correctly punctuated dialogue.

questions.q: Extend: write the rule for each error type you fixed.
questions.a: Rules for splices, apostrophes and speech.

questions.q: Stretch: use a semi-colon and a colon correctly in one paragraph.

questions.a: B) The dog wagged its tail.. 'its' shows possession without an apostrophe; 'it's' means 'it is'.

questions.q: Answer the ponder with your own most common error.
questions.a: Answers vary; comma splices are the most common.
